text:
Maya: Heads-up — saw a steady memory creep on long streaming sessions (tool-loop + multi-tool chat). Not classic sticky-residency; looks like lots of tiny freed KV pages not returning to slab pools. Attached a short flame and counters. cc @Sahil @Alex

Sahil: Can you paste the top-level counters and the pmap/heap snapshot?

Maya: quick counters: kv_pages_in_use: 132032 -> 141876 over ~2h, page_free_list_len: 48 -> 52 (weirdly low), slab_meta_free: 4200 -> 4120. Flame shows a lot of allocations from `kv_page_alloc_unaligned` and `batcher_write_prefix` paths. Link: https://perf.redwood/trace/3812345678

Alex: hmm — kernel fallback causing temp allocs would be at compute layer, but since flame points at batcher+kv allocs this smells like fragmentation from many small unique keys. Any batching heuristic changes recently?

Jun: Repro steps? Is this the longchat toolloop harness or a customer stream?

Maya: Repro is short: run long-toolloop with long context input and toolcalls enabled. Command I used:```bash
./bin/longchat --mode toolloop --seq 4096 --batch-size 1 --tool-batched true --prefetch off --duration 2h
```Observed growth starts after ~20m and is linear.

perf-bot: perf alert: similar trend detected in auto-test cluster on 2026-02-12 03:14 UTC (regression window overlapped with commit ae3f9c).

Sahil: I pulled a heap profile from your run: top alloc sites are `kv_page_alloc_unaligned`, `slab_meta_grow`, and `page_forwarding_record`. There's a lot of small (~512B-2KB) pages piling up. Could be page size fragmentation.

Alex: Two hypotheses: 1) batcher is splitting prefixes too eagerly, creating many tiny writes and unique page keys (worse locality). 2) a race in eviction/path forward updates leaves stale tiny pages that don't get reclaimed.

Maya: I added an extra debug log around `page_ref_update()` and saw repeated logs: "forwarded page with stale ref -> delayed_free_count++" ~3x/min.

Jun: That suggests a delayed pointer update path. We have async writeback that defers pointer swaps — if the free path doesn't re-link to the slab freelist immediately we can see short-lived runoffs that become long-lived if compaction doesn't catch them.

Sahil: Quick experiments: locally I bumped hot-window from 32 -> 128 (KV reuse heuristic) and enabled page coalescing branch (PR 4502). Results: growth rate dropped from ~9MB/h to ~1.2MB/h. Coalescing seemed to reduce number of unique small pages by ~70%.

Alex: Nice. Also try forcing kernel hint for KV tight path: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=kv_opt ./bin/longchat ...` — that reduces intermediate temporaries in our runtime which indirectly lowers churn.

Maya: I ran both changes together (kv_opt + coalesce + hot-window=128) overnight: growth ~0.8MB/h, still not zero. Heap shows a small steady tail of ~40k tiny pages labeled `runoff`.

Jun: We should add counters for: page_forward_pending, delayed_free_count, slab_compaction_runs, and batch_prefix_split_count. Add a gated debug build so we can run long 24h traces in CI without too much overhead. I'll take the counters.

Sahil: I'll prototype an adaptive coalescing policy: if small-page-ratio > 15% and compaction_lag > 5s, increase coalesce aggressiveness. Could be a runtime knob to mitigate until we fix the root race.

Maya: For immediate triage I'd like a minimal repro that reliably hits the delayed_free_count > 100 in ~6h. Jun/Alex/Sahil — can one of you assemble a reduced testcase (no external tools, single-node) and drop it in `eng-runtime/ci-long-run/`?

Alex: I'll take the reduced test. Plan: strip tools, synthesize long prefix churn, and run with and without kv_opt/coalesce to get diffs.

Jun: I'll add the counters and a small compaction trigger to the debug build.

Sahil: I'll work on the adaptive coalescer patch and bench.

Maya: Perfect — tag me when you have the 24h run results. If we can get delayed_free_count -> 0 with compaction + coalesce, we'll prepare a rollout with the knobs enabled. :thumbsup:

Alex: FYI I'll also grep for recent changes around `batcher:split_prefix_groups` in the regression window (ae3f9c) — might be the origin.

perf-bot: noted — creating a regression job linking ae3f9c -> current for longtoolloop 24h.

Maya: Thanks team. Short-term mitigations look promising, long-term fix likely a combination of eviction ordering + compaction + smarter batching. I'll update this thread with 24h results.
